# Sep 09, 05:00 PM
Date: 2026-09-10 | Duration: 48.66999816894531m

## Summary
The session explained how to create and run Growth Book experiments using stable user IDs and hash-based bucketing, equal traffic splits, namespaces, feature flags, and release plans. Traffic changes during live experiments can bias results, while namespaces help prevent conflicting exposure. Feature flags determine what users see and can apply targeting rules such as country or OS. The analysis discussion covered exposure events, fact tables, metrics, dimensions, Bayesian confidence intervals, health checks, and goal, secondary, and guardrail metrics. Rare events may require longer experiments to reduce uncertainty. Customer discussions covered migration support, experiment ideation, and escalation of complex statistical questions to data scientists. The team also reviewed limited Example App access and Cross Book as a richer presales and training environment managed by designated team members.

## Keywords
experimentation, feature flags, GrowthBook, Bayesian analysis, metric slices, namespaces
